questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road (paragraph 3)

(3) The bus coughed itself awake at dawn and lurched onto the desert road. Outside, the land lay flat and bleached, a vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on. Heat was already rising from the tarmac in trembling ribbons, and the few thorn bushes crouched low as if afraid of being noticed by the sun.

Identify a word or phrase from paragraph 3 that suggests the same idea as each of the following:
(a) the bus had difficulty starting [1]
(b) the landscape is empty and featureless [1]
ms: (a) “coughed (itself awake)” (1)
(b) “a vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on” (1) — allow “flat (and bleached)”
questions.model:
(a) “coughed itself awake”
(b) “a vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on”
questions.tip: Copy only the words that carry the idea — over-long quotations can lose the mark.

questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road

(3) The bus coughed itself awake at dawn and lurched onto the desert road. Outside, the land lay flat and bleached …
(6) … the passengers wilted in their seats, faces glazed with sweat.

Using your own words, explain what the writer means by each of these words as they are used in the text:
(a) lurched [1]
(b) bleached [1]
(c) wilted [1]
ms: (a) moved suddenly / jerkily / unsteadily (1)
(b) faded / drained of colour / made pale (by the sun) (1)
(c) became weak / limp / drooped / lost their energy (in the heat) (1)
questions.model:
(a) moved forward with a sudden, unsteady jerk
(b) faded and made pale by the sun
(c) became limp and weak, drooping from the heat
questions.tip: Explain the meaning in context; don’t repeat the word or a form of it.

questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road (paragraph 3)

“… the few thorn bushes crouched low as if afraid of being noticed by the sun.”

Explain the meaning and the effect of this phrase. [3]
ms: Meaning: the bushes are small/stunted and grow close to the ground (1)
Effect: personification — the bushes are like frightened people/animals hiding (1)
Effect: the sun becomes a threatening predator/enemy; the landscape feels hostile and dangerous (1)
Effect: prepares for the sun as a ‘tyrant’ later / suggests nothing can escape the heat (1)
questions.model: The bushes are small and grow low to the ground. By saying they “crouched … as if afraid”, the writer personifies them as frightened creatures trying to hide, which turns the sun into a predator hunting for victims. This makes the desert feel hostile and threatening, and it prepares the reader for the sun becoming a “tyrant” later in the passage.
questions.tip: Meaning first (what is literally happening), then effect (what the image makes us feel or imagine).

questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road (paragraph 6)

“It hammered on the metal roof until the whole bus rang like a struck pan … Even the driver’s radio gave up, its music dissolving into a hiss of static, as though the heat had melted the songs.”

Explain how the writer uses sound in these phrases to create effect. Refer to “rang like a struck pan” and “dissolving into a hiss of static”. [4]
ms: “rang like a struck pan” — meaning: the heat is so intense the roof seems to vibrate/ring (1)
Effect: simile suggests a loud, harsh, relentless noise; the bus becomes like a cooking pot — passengers are being cooked/trapped (1)
“dissolving into a hiss of static” — meaning: the radio stops playing music and only crackles (1)
Effect: ‘dissolving’/‘melted’ suggests even sound cannot survive the heat; ‘hiss’ is unpleasant, like something sizzling; comfort/entertainment disappears (1)
Link: both make the heat feel physical and overwhelming, affecting the senses (1)
questions.model:
“Rang like a struck pan” suggests the sun’s heat beats on the roof so hard that the bus seems to vibrate with noise. The simile turns the bus into a cooking pot, implying the passengers are trapped inside and being slowly cooked.
“Dissolving into a hiss of static” means the radio’s music fades into crackling. “Dissolving”, along with the idea that the heat “melted the songs”, suggests that even sound cannot survive the heat, and “hiss” sounds like something sizzling. Together the sounds make the heat feel loud, physical and inescapable.
questions.tip: When you discuss sound, say what the reader ‘hears’ and how it makes them feel.

questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road (paragraph 3)

(3) The bus coughed itself awake at dawn and lurched onto the desert road. Outside, the land lay flat and bleached, a vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on. Heat was already rising from the tarmac in trembling ribbons, and the few thorn bushes crouched low as if afraid of being noticed by the sun.

Choose three words or phrases from paragraph 3, including at least one image (but not the thorn bushes). Explain the meaning and effect of each. [6]
ms: Indicative content (other well-explained choices are credited):
“coughed itself awake” — the old bus starts noisily with difficulty; personified as a sick or sleepy old person, suggesting the bus is worn out and the journey will be hard
“lurched” — moves suddenly and unsteadily; suggests discomfort and lack of control, an uneasy start
“bleached” — colour drained by the sun; suggests the sun is so strong it has drained life from the land
“a vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on” — flat, blank, featureless land; suggests emptiness, nothing has happened here, abandoned/forgotten, making travellers feel tiny
“trembling ribbons” — heat haze shimmering; ‘trembling’ suggests nervousness/instability, ‘ribbons’ show the visible, wavy movement; the air itself seems alive and unsettling
Overall: an exhausted, empty, threatening landscape at the start of a hard journey

levels.d: Precise choices; meanings clear; effects explained in detail at word level (e.g. unpicking ‘forgotten’ or ‘trembling’); some sense of how the images build an overall impression.
Sensible choices with meanings mostly explained; effects identified but general (‘makes it vivid’).
Long or imprecise quotations; mostly meaning only, or devices named without explanation.

questions.model:
“Coughed itself awake” means the bus starts noisily and with difficulty. Personifying it as a sick old person waking up suggests the bus is worn out and that the journey ahead will be uncomfortable.
“A vast sheet of paper that someone had forgotten to write on” describes the flat, blank desert. “Vast” emphasises its size, while “forgotten” suggests the land has been abandoned, as if nothing has ever happened there – the passengers seem tiny and isolated in all that emptiness.
“Trembling ribbons” describes the heat haze rising from the road. “Ribbons” shows its wavy, visible shape, and “trembling” makes the air seem nervous and unstable, even though it is only dawn. Together the images create a tired, empty and slightly threatening world at the start of the journey.
questions.tip: Unpick single words inside an image (‘forgotten’, ‘trembling’) — that is what lifts an answer into the top level.

questions.q:
Text C – The Desert Road (paragraph 6)

(6) By midday the sun had become a tyrant. It hammered on the metal roof until the whole bus rang like a struck pan, and the passengers wilted in their seats, faces glazed with sweat. Even the driver’s radio gave up, its music dissolving into a hiss of static, as though the heat had melted the songs.

Explain how the writer uses language in paragraph 6 to convey the power of the sun. Choose three words or phrases and show how they work together to create an overall impression. [6]
ms: Indicative content:
“tyrant” — the sun is a cruel ruler with absolute power; the passengers are its helpless subjects; it is personal and deliberate
“hammered” — strikes repeatedly and violently; heat becomes a physical attack, continuous and noisy
“wilted” — passengers droop like plants without water; they are weakened/dehydrated, robbed of energy
“glazed with sweat” — faces shiny with sweat, like food glazed in an oven; links to the ‘pan’ image of being cooked
“the heat had melted the songs” — exaggeration: even something non-physical is destroyed; nothing can resist the sun
Overall: images link (tyrant → violence → victims; pan, glazed, melted → cooking) to show the sun as an all-powerful, cruel force; contrast with the quieter threat at dawn

levels.d: Precise choices; meanings clear; effects explored in detail; shows clearly how images connect (e.g. tyranny/violence or cooking) to create an overall impression.
Sensible choices and meanings; effects explained but more general; limited linking between images.
Mainly meanings, long quotations or techniques named without explaining their effect.

questions.model:
Calling the sun “a tyrant” presents it as a cruel ruler with total power, while the passengers become its helpless subjects. This idea of violence continues in “hammered”: the heat strikes the roof again and again, as if the sun is physically attacking the bus.
The passengers “wilted” like plants without water, showing that they are drained of strength and can only suffer. Their faces are “glazed with sweat”, which, together with the bus ringing “like a struck pan” and the heat that “melted the songs”, builds an image of cooking – the passengers are like food being slowly baked.
The overall impression is of an all-powerful, merciless sun. The writer combines images of tyranny and images of cooking to show that nothing – people, metal or even music – can resist it.
questions.tip: Finish with a sentence on the overall impression — it shows you understand how the choices work together.
